caption: An ice cream cone stands in a holder on a sunny picnic table, and the ice cream is melting and dripping down the side of the cone.
expectation: The ice cream sags and drips run downward and pool at the base; it never firms back up or drips upward.

caption: Hot water is poured from a kettle over a large block of ice on the ground, and the ice melts where the water hits it.
expectation: The surface turns wet and glossy and hollows where the hot water lands, meltwater runs down the block and pools on the ground, and faint steam may rise; the block may crack from the heat but does not grow, vanish all at once, or refreeze.

caption: A pat of cold butter is dropped into a hot frying pan, and it melts into a spreading pool of liquid.
expectation: The pat softens at the bottom first, slides and shrinks as it melts, and the liquid spreads outward; it does not stay a rigid block or re-solidify while the pan is hot.

caption: A pat of butter on a small plate is heated in a microwave and slowly melts.
expectation: The pat softens from the edges and bottom, slumps lower, and a glossy pool spreads outward on the plate as the pat shrinks; the butter does not stay a sharp-edged block, grow, vanish, or re-solidify while the microwave runs.

caption: A bowl of half-melted chocolate sits in a pan of steaming water and is stirred with a spatula, and the remaining pieces melt into the liquid.
expectation: The remaining pieces soften and lose their edges from the outside in and are smeared into the glossy liquid by the spatula; the melted part does not re-harden or break back into separate pieces while the water steams.

caption: A glowing red-hot metal ball is set on top of a large block of ice, and the ice melts around it.
expectation: The ice hisses and steams where the ball touches it, meltwater collects at the contact and the ball settles into a growing hollow; the ball's glow dims as it cools and the ice may crack; the ice does not stay untouched, the ball does not glow brighter or float free of the surface, and nothing refreezes while the ball is hot.

caption: A fruit popsicle stands upright on its stick in a cup on a sunny table, and it drips down the stick.
expectation: Drips run downward along the stick and collect in the cup; the popsicle looks glossy and soft and may slide on the stick; it does not refreeze, grow, or drip upward.

caption: Icicles hanging from a roof gutter drip steadily in the afternoon sun.
expectation: Water gathers at each tip and drops fall straight down; the icicles do not grow while dripping, and any change in length is a shortening.

caption: An ice cube is dropped into a mug of hot tea, and it melts quickly.
expectation: The cube floats, its edges round off and it shrinks steadily while faint steam rises from the tea; the tea level may rise slightly as it goes in; the cube does not grow, sink like a stone, vanish in a single frame, or stay sharp-cornered in hot liquid.

caption: A candle burns on a dinner table, and melted wax spills over the rim and runs down one side.
expectation: The pool sits at the top near the flame; the overflow runs downward and slows as it cools; the candle does not get taller and wax does not flow upward.

caption: A marshmallow on a stick is propped over a campfire, and it puffs, softens and sags.
expectation: The side facing the fire puffs and goes glossy first, then the marshmallow slumps and droops under its own weight, more on the fire side; the surface may brown, blacken in spots, or even catch if close to the flame, and any such darkening deepens and never fades back to white; it does not firm up again while over the heat.

caption: An ice cube is flicked onto a hot skillet, and it skitters around and shrinks as it melts.
expectation: The cube glides and spins on the hot surface with hissing steam, shrinking all the while; it does not sit still, grow, or stay the same size.

caption: A handful of shredded cheese is scattered onto a hot skillet, and the shreds melt and flow together into a bubbling layer.
expectation: The shreds slump and go glossy where they touch the pan first, then merge into one layer that bubbles at the edges; they do not stay as separate dry strands or pull back apart.

caption: A cube of cold butter is dropped into a bowl of hot soup, and the butter melts and spreads across the surface.
expectation: The cube floats and shrinks while a shiny film spreads out from it over the soup; it does not sink whole or stay solid.

caption: A small snowball is set on a hot griddle, and it hisses and collapses into water and steam.
expectation: The snow darkens and slumps from the bottom where it touches the metal, meltwater spreads and sizzles around it and steam rises; the ball does not stay white and firm, grow, or refreeze.

caption: A candle tips and a drop of liquid wax falls onto a wooden table, where it hardens into a small white disc.
expectation: The drop spreads slightly on landing, then stops moving and turns from clear to opaque as it sets; it does not keep flowing or become liquid again.

caption: Warm chocolate sauce is poured over a scoop of ice cream, and the sauce firms into a crackly shell on the cold surface.
expectation: The sauce flows down the scoop, slows, and stiffens where it touches the ice cream, turning dull; it does not keep running off the cold scoop.

caption: A bead of hot glue is squeezed from a glue gun onto a piece of wood, a button is pressed into it, and the glue sets hard around the button.
expectation: The glue comes out clear and runny, pulls a thin string as the gun lifts, and turns firm and cloudy within seconds; it does not stay runny.

caption: Boiling sugar syrup is drizzled from a spoon into a bowl of ice water, and the syrup hardens instantly into brittle golden threads.
expectation: The threads set the moment they hit the water and keep the shape they fell in; they do not dissolve, spread, or stay soft.

caption: A hairdryer is aimed at crayons taped to the top of a canvas, and the crayons melt and run down the canvas in coloured streaks that harden lower down.
expectation: The wax flows downward only while heated, slows as it cools away from the dryer, and stops as a raised hardened streak; it does not run upward or stay liquid at the bottom.

caption: Hot caramel is poured onto a cold marble slab, and the caramel spreads, then stiffens into a glassy sheet.
expectation: The caramel spreads while hot, slows, and stops moving as it sets; the sheet is rigid and can be cracked; it does not keep flowing off the slab.

caption: Melted butter is poured onto a plate that has just come out of the freezer, and the butter turns cloudy and firm on the plate.
expectation: The clear yellow liquid goes opaque pale and stops flowing within seconds of touching the cold plate; it does not stay glossy and runny.

caption: On a bitterly cold winter morning a cup of water is splashed onto a frozen car windshield, and the water freezes into a film of ice on the glass.
expectation: The water runs briefly and then stops, turning white and opaque where it freezes; the ice does not run off afterwards or clear the glass.

caption: Hot bacon fat is poured into a glass jar straight from the fridge, and the fat begins to set where it touches the cold glass.
expectation: Solid white forms first at the cold glass walls and creeps inward; the fat stops sloshing as it sets; it does not turn clear again.

caption: A frozen fish fillet is laid in a hot pan, and the white frost on its surface disappears as the fillet thaws.
expectation: The frost vanishes from the pan side first with a hiss and the fillet turns from stiff to limp; the frost does not return.

caption: A bag of frozen peas is emptied into a pot of hot water, and the frost on them vanishes and the clumps break apart.
expectation: The frozen clumps separate as they thaw and the peas sink or bob individually; the frost does not reappear.

caption: A wax crayon lies on a hot skillet, and it softens, slumps, and melts into a coloured pool.
expectation: The crayon sags and loses its shape from the side touching the pan, and a pool of the same colour spreads out from it; it does not stay stiff, straighten, or change colour.

caption: A block of frozen orange juice is dropped into a jug of hot water, and it melts, the orange colour spreading into the water.
expectation: The block rounds off and shrinks while orange streaks sink and spread from it and the water turns steadily more orange; the block does not grow and the water does not clear again.

caption: A spoonful of solid white coconut oil is dropped into a hot frying pan, and it melts into clear liquid.
expectation: The white lump turns glossy and clear from the bottom where it touches the pan and shrinks as a colourless pool spreads out around it; the pool stays clear with no foam or browning, and the oil does not stay white and solid or turn white again in the hot pan.

caption: A wedge of cheese sits under the heating element of a raclette grill, and the face nearest the element softens, sags and drips.
expectation: Only the face toward the heat softens and goes glossy; drips run downward off the lowest point onto the plate below; the far side stays firm and the cheese does not stiffen again under the heat.

caption: Warm water is poured over a frosted car windshield on a cold morning, and the frost clears where the water runs.
expectation: The frost turns clear along the path of the water and the water runs downward off the glass; frost does not re-form on the wetted glass while the water is warm, and untouched areas stay frosted.

caption: A handful of chocolate chips is dropped into a saucepan of hot cream, and the chips melt into the cream.
expectation: The chips soften, lose their sharp edges and go glossy, sinking or smearing into the cream while dark streaks spread through the pale cream; the chips do not stay hard-edged, float unchanged, or re-harden in the hot cream.

caption: A square of chocolate lies in a skillet over low heat, and it melts into a spreading pool.
expectation: The square goes glossy and sags from the bottom, its edges round off and a pool spreads out around it; it does not keep sharp edges, re-harden in the warm pan, or turn pale.

caption: Hot espresso is poured over a scoop of vanilla ice cream in a glass, and the ice cream melts.
expectation: The scoop softens and shrinks where the hot coffee runs over it, and pale melted cream runs down and streaks into the dark coffee at the bottom of the glass; the scoop does not stay a firm ball, grow, or refreeze in the hot liquid.

caption: A soap bubble rests on a snow-covered railing in bitter cold, and feathery ice crystals spread across its surface until the whole bubble has frozen white.
expectation: The crystals start at a few points and spread across the film within seconds, turning it from clear to frosted; the bubble keeps its shape while it freezes; the frost does not retreat and the bubble does not clear again.

caption: A bottle of water taken from a very cold freezer while still liquid is tapped against a table, and the water inside turns to slush from the top down within seconds.
expectation: The ice starts at one spot and spreads through the liquid as a cloudy front; the bottle keeps its shape and the slush does not turn back into clear water.

caption: Two identical ice cubes sit side by side, one on a thick metal block and one on a plastic block, and the cube on the metal is melting faster in a spreading pool.
expectation: The cube on the metal shrinks and rounds off sooner and its puddle grows larger than the one on the plastic; neither cube grows, and the difference does not reverse.

caption: Molten candle wax is dripped from a spoon into a bowl of cold water, and each drop hardens into a pale bead that floats.
expectation: Each drop goes from clear and runny to opaque and solid within a moment of touching the water, keeps the shape it landed in, and floats; the beads do not dissolve, spread out, or melt back together.

caption: Ice cubes are dropped into a glass of warm cola, and they crack with a snap as they hit the liquid, splitting and fizzing.
expectation: Cracks appear on the cubes within a moment of entering the warm liquid and some cubes split; the pieces float and begin to shrink; the cubes do not stay glassy and whole or fuse back together.

caption: Coarse salt is scattered over an icy doorstep, and the ice pits and turns to slush where the grains land.
expectation: Small hollows form around each grain and spread, the surface goes wet and grey, and the untouched ice stays hard and clear; the pits do not heal over.

caption: Molten sealing wax is dripped onto the flap of an envelope and a metal stamp is pressed into the pool, and the wax sets hard with the stamped pattern within seconds.
expectation: The wax spreads while liquid, takes the stamp's pattern, and stops moving as it hardens and dulls; the pattern stays sharp and the wax does not flow again after the stamp lifts.

caption: A cube of jelly sits on a plate resting over a pan of steaming water, and it slumps and melts into a puddle.
expectation: The cube softens and sags from the bottom and edges, its corners round off and a clear puddle of the same colour spreads out; it does not firm up again while the plate is hot.

caption: Thick white icing is piped onto cinnamon rolls fresh from the oven, and it softens and runs down into the gaps between them.
expectation: The icing loses its piped ridges, goes glossy and thin, and flows downward off the high points; it does not hold its shape or run uphill.

caption: A car's frosted side mirror is switched to heat on a cold morning, and the frost turns to droplets in a patch that spreads across the glass.
expectation: The clearing starts in one area and spreads outward, the white frost turning wet and then clear; frost does not re-form on the cleared glass while the heater runs.

caption: Two wet ice cubes straight from the freezer are pressed together for a moment and let go, and they stay stuck as one piece.
expectation: After release the cubes hold together and can be lifted as one; they do not fall apart, slide off each other, or melt open at the join while they stay cold.

caption: A kettle on a stove is at the boil, steam pours from the spout, and the lid rattles.
expectation: Steam rises and spreads upward from the spout, thinning as it goes; the rattle coincides with the steam; steam does not sink or flow downward.

caption: A pot of pasta water boils over on a stove, and foamy water spills down the outside of the pot onto the burner.
expectation: Foam rises inside the pot, climbs over the rim, and runs down the outside, hissing on the burner; the level inside drops as it spills; foam does not fall back into the pot from above.

caption: A saucepan of water on high heat is at a rolling boil, with large bubbles bursting at the surface.
expectation: Bubbles form at the bottom and rise to burst at the top, the surface churns, and wisps of steam rise; bubbles do not sink or form at the surface and travel down.

caption: The lid is lifted off a rice cooker, and a cloud of steam billows up out of it.
expectation: The steam escapes upward the moment the lid comes off, spreads, and thins; it does not pour down the sides or stay in the cooker.

caption: A steam wand is pushed into a jug of milk, and the milk hisses, swirls, and rises in the jug as foam.
expectation: The foam builds from the top of the milk while the wand runs and stops rising when the wand is switched off; the milk level does not drop.

caption: A pressure cooker on a stove starts hissing, and a jet of steam shoots up from the valve on its lid.
expectation: The jet goes straight up from the valve, spreading as it rises, and the hissing lasts as long as the jet; steam does not come from the sealed rim.

caption: A pot of soup simmers on a stove, with small bubbles breaking the surface and steam rising.
expectation: Bubbles appear from below and pop at the surface, the surface shifts gently, and steam rises; the soup does not go still while the heat stays on.

caption: Eggs boil in a pot on a stove, rattling against each other as the water bubbles around them.
expectation: The eggs jostle only because of the bubbling water, staying at the bottom; steam rises above the pot; the eggs do not float up or stay perfectly still in a boiling pot.

caption: A steam iron is pressed onto a shirt on an ironing board, and puffs of steam rise from around the iron.
expectation: Steam comes out only while the iron is on the fabric and rises from its edges; the fabric under the iron flattens; steam does not pour downward.

caption: Steam rises from a manhole cover on a city street on a cold morning.
expectation: The steam comes up through the holes and drifts upward, thinning and bending with the breeze; it does not flow along the ground like water.

caption: Boiling water is poured from a kettle into a mug, and steam rises from the mug as it fills.
expectation: Steam rises from the falling stream and from the mug's surface, growing as the mug fills; the water itself falls downward and the steam goes up.

caption: Noodles cook in a pot of boiling water, bobbing and swirling with the bubbles.
expectation: The noodles move with the churning water and settle when the heat is turned down; they do not move on their own in still water.

caption: Water boils in a glass electric kettle, with streams of bubbles rising from the bottom to the surface.
expectation: Bubbles start at the heated base and travel upward, growing as they rise, and steam leaves the top; bubbles do not travel downward.

caption: A divided hot pot with spicy red oil broth on one side and clear broth on the other heats over a burner, and the red side comes to the boil while the clear side stays calm.
expectation: Large bubbles rise and burst through the red oil layer and its surface churns, while the clear side stays nearly flat with at most a few tiny bubbles and faint steam; the two broths stay on their own sides of the divider and keep their colours; the red side does not fall quiet while the burner is on, and the clear side does not boil harder than the red side.

caption: Water is ladled onto the hot stones of a sauna, and a burst of steam rises off the stones with a hiss.
expectation: The water hisses and vanishes into steam almost at once, the steam rises and fills the upper room; water does not remain pooled on the hot stones.

caption: The lid of a large pot of dumplings is lifted at a street stall, and steam rolls up out of the pot into the cold air.
expectation: Steam rises and hangs visibly in the cold air before fading; the dumplings sit in bubbling water below; steam does not sink.

caption: A dishwasher door is opened at the end of its cycle, and a wave of steam rolls up and out of the machine.
expectation: The steam escapes upward past the door and thins; the dishes inside are wet and hot; steam does not flow down onto the floor.

caption: A coffee pot on a warming plate is nearly empty, and the last of the coffee bubbles and steams in the bottom.
expectation: Small bubbles form and burst in the shallow liquid, steam rises, and the level drops further; the coffee does not increase in volume.

caption: A pan of water on a stove is at a boil, and the burner is turned off; the bubbling dies down and only faint steam remains.
expectation: The churning stops within seconds of the heat going off and steam fades gradually; the water does not keep boiling with no heat or stop instantly.

caption: A geyser in a national park erupts, sending a column of boiling water and steam high into the air before it falls back.
expectation: The water rises as a column, slows at the top, and falls back down around the vent while the steam keeps drifting upward and away.

caption: Wet spinach is tossed into a very hot pan, and a burst of steam rises with a loud hiss as the leaves wilt.
expectation: The steam rises the moment the wet leaves touch the pan; the leaves shrink and go limp within seconds and do not spring back.

caption: A locomotive at a heritage railway lets off steam, and a great white cloud rolls up from beside the wheels.
expectation: The cloud bursts out and rises, thinning as it spreads; it does not sink and lie along the track.

caption: Water is poured onto the hot coals of a barbecue after cooking, and a hissing cloud of steam rises from the grill.
expectation: Steam rises in a burst where the water hits and the coals darken and stop glowing there; the water does not stay pooled on hot coals.

caption: A hot pot bubbles in the centre of a dinner table, and thin slices of meat dropped into the broth curl up and rise to the surface.
expectation: Steam rises from the broth, the slices curl and float up within seconds, and the broth keeps bubbling; the slices do not sink and lie flat.

caption: A jet of steam from a wallpaper steamer plate softens old wallpaper, and the paper peels away in wet strips.
expectation: Steam escapes upward around the plate's edges; the paper darkens and loosens only where steamed; the strips hang and fall downward.

caption: Rain falls on a sun-baked road, and steam rises from the hot asphalt as the drops hit.
expectation: The rain falls downward and the steam rises upward off the surface; wet patches spread and the steaming fades as the road cools.

caption: A glowing piece of metal is plunged into a bucket of water, and a cloud of steam bursts up from the bucket.
expectation: The steam erupts the instant the metal enters, rises, and fades; the metal loses its glow in the water and does not glow again.

caption: A ladle of hot broth is poured over cold noodles in a bowl, and a puff of steam rises from the bowl.
expectation: Steam rises where the hot broth lands; the broth flows down around the noodles; the puff thins as the bowl cools.

caption: Boiling water is poured over a tea bag in a glass, and steam rises while the colour spreads from the bag.
expectation: Steam rises from the glass; the colour drifts out of the bag into the water and does not gather back into the bag.

caption: A car with an overheated engine sits at the roadside with steam pouring out from under the hood.
expectation: The steam escapes upward from the edges of the hood and grille and drifts away; it does not run down the front of the car.

caption: A lid is lifted from a pan of steamed vegetables, and steam rises to fog the range hood above.
expectation: The steam rises straight to the hood and spreads under it; the hood's metal fogs where the steam touches; steam does not sink toward the counter.

caption: A saucepan of milk on a stove begins to boil, and the milk foams up rapidly toward the rim.
expectation: The foam rises quickly and climbs the sides, threatening to spill; if the pan is lifted off the heat the foam sinks back; it does not stay as a static layer.

caption: A vent pipe on a factory roof releases a steady plume of white steam into the winter sky.
expectation: The plume rises from the pipe, bends with the wind, and thins with distance; it does not fall back onto the roof.

caption: Frozen french fries are dropped into a pot of hot oil, and the oil erupts in bubbles and steam.
expectation: The bubbling starts the moment the fries go in and is fiercest at first, easing as the frost is gone; steam rises; the oil level rises with the fries.

caption: A glass electric kettle at a rolling boil clicks off, and the churning bubbles die down and the steam thins.
expectation: The streams of bubbles from the base stop within moments of the click and the surface settles, while the steam from the spout weakens gradually; the water does not keep boiling hard with the element off or fall still in a single frame.

caption: A garment steamer is run slowly down a wrinkled shirt hanging on a rail, and the creases relax and drop out where the steam passes.
expectation: Steam rises from the steamer head, the fabric darkens slightly with moisture and smooths only along the path the head has taken; creases do not come back once steamed and untreated areas stay wrinkled.

caption: A basket of laundry fresh from a hot dryer is set outside on a freezing morning, and vapour rises off the warm clothes.
expectation: The vapour rises from the clothes and thins as it drifts; it is thickest at first and fades as the clothes cool; it does not sink or gather on the ground.

caption: A spoonful of salt is tipped into a pot of boiling water, and the water froths up sharply for a moment before settling back to a rolling boil.
expectation: The surge of foam comes at the moment the salt goes in and climbs the sides, then dies back within seconds; the water does not froth before the salt goes in or stay frothed.

caption: A baked potato fresh from the oven is split open with a fork, and steam rises from the white flesh inside.
expectation: The steam appears the moment the potato is opened, rises from the cut faces and thins; it does not come from the unbroken skin or sink onto the plate.

caption: A cold bottle of soda has just been taken out of the fridge on a hot day, and beads of water form on the outside of the bottle.
expectation: A haze appears first, then droplets grow and some run downward, leaving trails; the beads do not appear on the inside of the bottle or vanish while it stays cold.

caption: Breath is blown onto a cold window pane, and a patch of fog appears on the glass and then fades.
expectation: The fog appears where the breath hits, exactly during the exhale, and clears from the edges inward over a few seconds; it does not appear before the breath.

caption: A pair of glasses is brought in from the cold street into a warm café, and the lenses fog over.
expectation: The fog appears on the lenses within a moment of entering and does not appear while they are still outside; any later change is toward clearing.

caption: A glass of ice water sits on a wooden table in a warm room, and condensation runs down the outside of the glass onto the table.
expectation: Droplets on the outside run down and feed the ring; the ring does not shrink while the glass stays cold; the water does not come from inside the glass.

caption: A hot shower runs with the bathroom door closed, and the bathroom window is misting over from the bottom up.
expectation: The mist thickens while the shower runs and heavier drops run downward in streaks; the glass does not clear while the shower runs.

caption: A chest freezer is opened, and a low mist rolls out over the rim and sinks toward the floor.
expectation: The mist spills over the edge and downward, hugging the freezer's sides and thinning as it falls; it does not rise like steam.

caption: The lid of a pot that has been simmering is lifted and turned over, and its underside is covered in drops that run and drip off.
expectation: Drops cover the inner face of the lid and fall from the lowest edge as it tilts; the drops do not stay put on a tilted lid.

caption: A man exhales on a frosty morning, and his breath appears as a white cloud that drifts away and fades.
expectation: The cloud appears just in front of his mouth on each exhale, spreads, and disappears within a second or two; it is not visible when he inhales.

caption: A tub of ice cream is taken from the freezer, and a white frost forms on its lid as it sits on the counter.
expectation: The frost appears as a growing white haze on the cold surfaces, then turns to water droplets as the tub warms; it does not appear on the warm counter.

caption: A frosted beer mug is filled from a tap on a warm terrace, and the outside of the mug beads with water.
expectation: The frost turns to droplets that run down the glass and wet the table; the beads grow while the mug is cold.

caption: Steam from a kettle rises against a kitchen cabinet door, and the door beads with water that runs down.
expectation: Water forms on the door where the steam hits and runs downward in drips; the water does not form on the hot kettle.

caption: A lid is snapped onto a container of hot food, and the inside of the clear lid fogs over.
expectation: The fog forms on the inner surface of the lid within moments and thickens into drops; the outside stays clear.

caption: A camera is carried from an air-conditioned lobby out into humid summer heat, and its lens fogs up.
expectation: The fog appears on the cold lens shortly after stepping outside and clears as the camera warms; it does not appear while still indoors.

caption: A motorcyclist stops at a light on a cold day, and the inside of the helmet visor fogs with each breath.
expectation: The fog thickens with each exhale and thins between breaths; when the visor is lifted it clears.

caption: Sunlight warms a greenhouse in the morning, and the inside of its glass panes is covered in drops that begin to run down.
expectation: The drops merge and streak downward on the inner surface; the glass gradually clears from the top as the day warms.

caption: A car's air conditioning is turned to full blast on a humid day, and faint mist drifts out of the dashboard vents.
expectation: The mist appears at the vents and disappears within a short distance into the cabin air; it does not pool or pour like liquid.

caption: A cold metal water pipe runs along a basement wall on a humid day, and it sweats droplets that drip onto the floor.
expectation: Drops form along the underside of the pipe and fall straight down, leaving a wet line on the floor; water does not appear on the warm wall.

caption: Steam from a hot shower drifts against the cool tiled wall, and the tiles bead with water that runs in streaks.
expectation: Drops form on the tiles, join, and run downward; the tiles look wet only where the steam reaches.

caption: A hot dishwasher is opened and the steam that escapes fogs the cool kitchen window above the sink.
expectation: The fog forms on the window where the rising steam reaches it and clears over time; it does not form on the warm dishwasher.

caption: A cold bottle of milk is poured into a glass on a hot patio, and the outside of the glass mists over.
expectation: The mist appears on the glass up to the level of the cold milk and beads into drops that run down; above the milk line it stays clearer.

caption: A pair of glasses is carried into a steam room, and the lenses cloud over completely within seconds.
expectation: The lenses go white and opaque almost at once and stay fogged while in the steam.

caption: A cold pane of glass is held over a steaming kettle, and it fogs and then drips from its lower edge.
expectation: Fog forms on the underside facing the steam, gathers into drops, and drips from the lowest edge; the top face stays dry.

caption: Breath is blown onto a cold hand mirror, and the fog on the glass hides the reflection for a moment before it clears.
expectation: The fog appears with the breath, blurs the reflection, and clears from the edges within seconds; the reflection returns unchanged.

caption: A cold metal railing on a humid summer morning is covered in fine droplets, and a finger drags through them leaving a clear line.
expectation: The line stays clear where the finger passed while the surrounding droplets remain; the droplets do not vanish from the untouched area.

caption: A tray of ice cubes is taken from the freezer, and the cubes and tray frost over white.
expectation: The white frost appears first on the coldest surfaces; any later change is toward wetness as the tray warms, and the frost does not vanish and return.

caption: A dog waits alone in a parked car on a cold evening, and the windows fog up from the inside as it pants.
expectation: The fog forms on the inside face of the glass, thickest near the dog and toward the top, and grows while the dog pants; it does not form on the outside of the windows or clear while the car stays shut.

caption: A car's defroster is switched on against a windshield fogged from the inside, and a clear patch spreads upward from the vents.
expectation: The glass clears first just above the dashboard vents and the clear area grows upward and outward; the fog does not thicken while the defroster runs and does not clear from the top down.

caption: Chunks of dry ice are dropped into a punch bowl of water, and thick white fog boils up, spills over the rim and sinks toward the table.
expectation: The fog rises out of the bowl, pours over the rim, flows down the outside and spreads along the table, thinning as it goes, while the water bubbles; it does not drift up to the ceiling like steam.

caption: Liquid nitrogen is poured into a metal bowl, and a cloud of white fog rolls over the rim and cascades down the sides.
expectation: The liquid boils violently in the bowl and the fog spills downward over the edge, hugging the surface it falls onto and thinning as it spreads; the fog does not drift upward like steam.

caption: The glass door of a supermarket freezer is closed after being held open, and the inside of the glass fogs over, then slowly clears as the cold air circulates.
expectation: The fog forms on the inner face of the door within moments of closing and fades gradually from the edges or the vents; it does not form on the outside or vanish all at once.

caption: A steel cocktail shaker filled with ice is shaken, and its outside turns white with frost within seconds.
expectation: The frost appears as a white haze that spreads over the metal while it is cold, thickest where the ice is inside; it turns to wet droplets as the shaker warms and does not appear on the warm parts.

caption: A chilled bottle of sparkling water is uncapped, and a small puff of white mist rises from its neck and vanishes.
expectation: The mist appears at the instant the cap comes off, rises a little above the neck and fades within a second; it does not appear before the cap is off or keep pouring out.

caption: A sheet of newspaper is laid over a campfire, and the paper catches, curls, blackens, and falls apart into ash.
expectation: The flame spreads across the paper from where it touched the fire, the paper curls and shrinks as it burns, and grey flakes drift down; the paper does not return or burn from a spot the flame never reached.

caption: A candle on a table is blown out, and a thin trail of smoke rises from the wick.
expectation: The flame leans away from the puff of breath and goes out during it; the smoke rises straight up and drifts; the candle does not relight on its own.

caption: A match is struck against the side of its box, and it flares into a flame that settles to a steady burn.
expectation: The flame appears at the head at the moment of the strike, flares, then burns steadily pointing upward while the matchstick blackens behind it.

caption: A dry log is tossed onto a campfire, and a burst of sparks flies up into the night.
expectation: Sparks rise with the hot air, drift, and go out within seconds; the flames climb around the new log; sparks do not fall as bright points to the ground.

caption: Wind gusts across a campfire, and the flames lean over and stretch out sideways before standing up again.
expectation: The flames bend in the direction the wind blows and return to pointing upward when the gust passes; they do not lean into the wind.

caption: A stick of incense is lit in a quiet room, and a thin ribbon of smoke rises from its tip and curls in the still air.
expectation: The smoke rises in a thin steady stream that wavers and spreads higher up; the tip glows red; the stick does not lengthen and the smoke does not sink.

caption: A long barbecue lighter is clicked, and a small flame appears at its tip and burns steadily.
expectation: The flame appears at the click, points upward regardless of how the lighter is tilted, and disappears when the trigger is released.

caption: The glowing embers in a fireplace are poked with a poker, and they brighten and send up a swirl of sparks.
expectation: The embers glow brighter where disturbed, sparks rise and fade, and the glow settles again afterwards; the embers do not turn back into unburnt wood.

caption: The knob on a gas stove is turned, and a ring of blue flames lights around the burner.
expectation: The flames appear all around the ring within a moment of the click, stand upright, and grow or shrink as the knob is turned; they vanish when it is turned off.

caption: A metal snuffer is lowered over a candle flame, and the flame dies and smoke curls out from under the snuffer.
expectation: The flame goes out within a moment of being covered, and smoke leaks out and rises when the snuffer is lifted; the flame does not keep burning under the cap.

caption: A bucket of water is poured over a dying campfire, and the fire goes out with a hiss in a cloud of steam and smoke.
expectation: The flames vanish where the water lands, a thick cloud rises and thins, and the wet ash stays dark; the fire does not flare back up.

caption: A lit sparkler stands upright in a cake, throwing off a spray of bright sparks that fade as they fall.
expectation: Sparks fly outward and downward from the burning point and go dark within a short distance; the burning point moves down the wire, never back up, and the spent wire above it is dark.

caption: A kerosene lamp is lit with a match, and the wick catches and the flame steadies inside the glass chimney.
expectation: The flame starts at the wick where the match touches, stands upright inside the glass, and keeps burning after the match is withdrawn.

caption: A match is set to a pile of dry leaves, and the fire spreads across the pile with smoke rising from it.
expectation: The flames spread outward from the lit spot, leaves blacken and shrink into ash, and smoke rises; burnt leaves do not become whole again.

caption: A charcoal chimney starter is lit, and flames and smoke rise up through the coals from the paper burning below.
expectation: The fire climbs upward through the chimney and smoke pours out of the top; the flames do not start at the top.

caption: A fatty burger is flipped on a grill, and fat drips onto the coals and a flame flares up under the patty.
expectation: The flare appears where the fat lands and dies back after a moment; the flames go upward around the patty.

caption: Air is blown gently onto the embers of a fire, and they glow brighter and a small flame springs up.
expectation: The embers brighten while the air blows and the flame appears at the brightest spot; the glow eases when the blowing stops.

caption: A lid is slid over a small grease fire in a pan, and the flames go out.
expectation: The flames die within moments of the lid covering the pan and smoke seeps from the edges; the fire does not keep burning under the lid.

caption: Smoke drifts from a chimney on a windy day and is blown sideways as it leaves the stack.
expectation: The smoke rises a little then streams downwind, in the same direction as trees and flags bend; it does not go against the wind.

caption: A bonfire on a beach burns high, and sparks and embers rise into the dark sky and wink out.
expectation: The sparks climb with the hot air, drift, and go dark high above the fire; the flames point upward and lean with the sea breeze.

caption: A blowtorch heats a copper pipe, and the flame roars out of the nozzle in a blue cone.
expectation: The flame points in the direction the torch is aimed, appears and disappears with the valve, and the pipe darkens where it is heated.

caption: A hose sprays water onto a burning shed, and the flames shrink and the smoke turns from black to white steam.
expectation: The flames die where the water lands and rising steam replaces the dark smoke; the fire does not grow while being doused.

caption: A lit sparkler is dropped into a bucket of water, and it goes out with a hiss and a puff of steam.
expectation: The sparks stop as the sparkler enters the water, a small cloud rises, and the wire sinks dark; it does not keep sparking under water.

caption: A campfire is fed with damp wood, and thick white smoke pours off the logs while the flames struggle.
expectation: The smoke rises thickly and drifts with the wind; the flames stay small and flicker; the smoke does not settle to the ground.

caption: A row of tea-light candles is lit one after another with a long match, and each flame stands upright after it catches.
expectation: Each candle lights only when the match touches it and stays lit afterwards; none lights before being touched or goes out on its own.

caption: Brandy is ignited in a pan, and a sheet of flame rises above the pan and then dies down.
expectation: The flame rises upward from the surface, burns for a few seconds, and shrinks away; it does not sink into the pan or come back once gone.

caption: A magnifying glass focuses sunlight onto a dry leaf until a wisp of smoke appears and a small glowing spot begins to spread.
expectation: The smoke rises from the bright spot; the dark scorched patch grows outward from that spot and does not shrink.

caption: A wooden skewer is dropped into the grill's coals and catches fire.
expectation: The skewer lights where it touches the coals, the flame runs along it, and it blackens and shrinks behind the flame; it does not return to pale wood.

caption: A gust blows across a row of candles on a windowsill, and the flames bend sideways and two of them go out, leaving smoke trails.
expectation: All the flames lean the same way with the gust; the ones that go out smoke upward; the survivors straighten after the gust.

caption: A handful of dry pine needles is fed to a small fire, and they crackle and flare up brightly before the flames settle.
expectation: The flare comes as the needles land and rises upward, then dies back to the size before; the needles become ash and do not reappear.

caption: A candle inside a glass jar has burned down to its last pool of wax, and the flame goes out.
expectation: The flame is small, dies, and smoke rises from the wick; the wax does not refill and the flame does not return.

caption: A lit match is dropped into a fire pit filled with kindling, and the fire catches and grows from the bottom up.
expectation: The flames start where the match lands and spread upward through the kindling; smoke rises; the fire does not start at the top or everywhere at once.

caption: A candle is set beside an open window on a windy night, and its flame streams sideways and flickers wildly.
expectation: The flame leans away from the window in the direction the curtain blows and dances with each gust; it never leans toward the wind.

caption: A fire steel is scraped with a knife, and sparks shower onto a nest of dry tinder that begins to smoke and then flame.
expectation: The sparks fall downward onto the tinder, smoke rises from where they land, and a small flame follows the smoke; nothing burns before the sparks land.

caption: A glass jar is lowered over a burning tea light on a plate, and the flame shrinks and goes out within seconds, leaving a wisp of smoke inside the jar.
expectation: The flame gets smaller and dimmer after the jar comes down and then dies; the smoke rises and hangs inside the jar; the flame does not keep burning at full size or relight.

caption: A slice of bread sits in a running toaster, and its top edge darkens and thin smoke begins to rise from the slots.
expectation: The darkening deepens over time and never lightens; smoke rises from the slots only after the bread has darkened; the bread does not turn pale again.

caption: The vents on a charcoal grill's bowl are slid shut, and the bright orange coals dim to a dull glow.
expectation: The glow fades gradually after the vents close and does not flare back up while they stay shut; the coals do not brighten or go dark in a single frame.

caption: A sheet of paper rests on a wire rack above a burning candle, and a brown spot forms over the flame, then a hole burns through with a glowing edge spreading outward.
expectation: The brown patch appears first and darkens, the hole opens at its centre and grows outward with a glowing rim and thin smoke; the hole does not shrink and the paper does not turn white again.

caption: A struck match stands upright in a holder and burns down, the flame creeping down the stick as the burnt part above it blackens and curls.
expectation: The flame moves downward along the stick, the wood behind it turns black and bends, and the flame shrinks as it nears the base; the burnt part does not turn pale again and the flame does not climb back up.

caption: A metal spoon rests across a stand with its bowl just above a candle flame, and black soot builds up on the underside where the flame touches.
expectation: The black patch appears only where the flame licks the metal and grows darker and wider over time; it does not appear elsewhere on the spoon or fade while the flame is there.

caption: A burning log in a fireplace cracks with a pop, and a few sparks jump out onto the hearth and go dark.
expectation: The sparks leave the log at the pop, fly outward and downward, and fade within a second or two of landing; they do not rise to the ceiling or keep glowing on the stone.

caption: A lit candle in a holder is tilted to one side, and the flame keeps pointing straight up while melted wax runs down the low side.
expectation: The flame stays vertical whatever the candle's angle and the wax runs down the lower edge and drips off it; the flame does not lean with the candle and the wax does not run uphill.

caption: Dumplings that have cooked in a pot of boiling water bob up to the surface one by one.
expectation: The dumplings rise one by one from the bottom and stay bobbing at the surface; none sinks again once up.

caption: Popcorn kernels in a covered pot with hot oil begin to pop, jumping and turning into fluffy white pieces that fill the pot.
expectation: Each kernel bursts suddenly into a much larger piece and jumps; the pot fills from the bottom up; popped pieces do not shrink back into kernels.

caption: Chestnuts roast in a pan over a fire, and their shells split open with a crack.
expectation: Each shell cracks along a line and gapes open, the nut inside showing; the split does not close again.

caption: A plastic spoon left resting on the rim of a hot frying pan droops and bends over the edge.
expectation: The spoon softens only where it touches the hot rim and sags downward under its own weight; it does not straighten while still hot.

caption: A strip of tissue paper is held above a hot radiator, and it lifts and flutters upward in the warm air.
expectation: The strip rises and dances only above the radiator and hangs still when moved away; it does not fall straight down over the heat.

caption: A hot oven door is opened, and the air above the opening shimmers and wavers.
expectation: The shimmer rises out of the oven and is strongest directly above the opening, fading with height; it does not flow down toward the floor.

caption: Wet chicken pieces are dropped into a pan of hot oil, and the oil spits and crackles violently for a moment.
expectation: The spitting starts the instant the wet food touches the oil, throws droplets upward and outward, and eases as the surface water is gone.

caption: A marshmallow in a microwave swells to several times its size and then collapses when the door opens.
expectation: It puffs up gradually while heating and sinks back into a sticky blob once the heat stops; it does not stay puffed.

caption: A paper pinwheel is held above a lit candle, and it begins to spin in the rising warm air.
expectation: The spinning begins when the pinwheel is over the flame and stops when it is moved away; it does not spin over an unlit candle.

caption: A heat gun is aimed at the loose plastic wrap around a gift basket, and the wrap tightens and shrinks snugly around the basket.
expectation: The film pulls tight and smooth where the heat is applied and stays tight afterwards; it does not loosen again.

caption: Sausages sizzle in a hot pan, and one of them splits open along its side with a pop.
expectation: The skin bursts along a line and the split gapes open, juices escaping; the skin does not close again.

caption: A dented ping-pong ball is dropped into a bowl of very hot water, and the dent pops back out.
expectation: The dent pushes out within seconds of the ball entering the hot water and the ball floats round; the dent does not return in the hot water.

caption: A hot air balloon's burner is fired, and the balloon lifts off the field.
expectation: The balloon rises while the burner fires and drifts slowly; it does not lift before the burner runs or drop as soon as it stops.

caption: A plastic soda bottle is left too close to a campfire, and the near side shrivels and caves in.
expectation: The plastic facing the fire wrinkles and pulls inward; the far side keeps its shape; the caved side does not pop back out.

caption: A few drops of water are flicked onto a hot griddle, and the drops skitter around and vanish.
expectation: The drops dance across the surface and disappear within seconds; they do not sit still or grow.

caption: A lidded plastic container of leftovers is heated in a microwave, and the lid domes upward and pops loose.
expectation: The lid bulges more and more as the food heats, then lifts at one corner with a puff of steam; it does not sink inward.

caption: Heat rises from a barbecue grill on a summer afternoon, and the view of the fence behind it wavers in the shimmering air.
expectation: The shimmer sits above the grill and rises, fading with height; the fence is distorted only through the hot air above the grill.

caption: Cooking oil is poured into a pan over high heat, and the oil begins to shimmer and ripple across its surface.
expectation: The surface goes from still to moving in fine ripples as the pan heats and thin wisps of smoke may rise; the ripples do not appear in a cold pan.

caption: A handful of dry rice noodles is dropped into hot water, and they go from stiff and brittle to limp and floppy.
expectation: The noodles soften from the ends touching the water and sink into loose coils; they do not stiffen again in the hot water.

caption: Hot water is poured over a pot of dried seaweed, and the crisp sheets swell and soften into flowing strands.
expectation: The sheets expand and become slippery and limp within moments; they do not return to crisp flat sheets in the water.

caption: A flour tortilla lies on a wire rack over a gas flame, and pockets of the tortilla puff up into bubbles.
expectation: The bubbles rise on the upper side while the tortilla is over the flame and the underside browns in spots; the puffed pockets do not appear before heating and the browning does not fade.

caption: A damp sock hangs from a stick propped beside a campfire, and steam rises from it.
expectation: Steam rises from the side of the sock facing the fire and drifts upward with the heat; the sock does not become wetter and the vapour does not sink.

caption: Bacon strips laid in a hot pan begin to sizzle, and the strips shrink and curl at the edges.
expectation: The strips get shorter and their edges lift and buckle as they cook; fat pools around them; the strips do not flatten or grow.

caption: A hairdryer is aimed at a bent plastic pipe, and the pipe softens enough to be straightened by hand and holds its new shape when cool.
expectation: The pipe bends only where heated, moves under the hands while warm, and stays put after cooling; it does not spring back to its old bend.

caption: A frozen block of soup sits in a pan over heat, sliding around on a thin layer of melt and shrinking as the liquid pools around it.
expectation: The block loosens from the pan, glides slightly when the pan is tilted, and gets smaller as the pool grows; the pool does not refreeze.

caption: A lava lamp that has warmed up glows on a table, and the blobs of wax inside rise and sink.
expectation: Blobs rise from the bottom, slow near the top, and fall again in a slow cycle; they do not jump or move in a way unrelated to the warm base.

caption: A pat of cold butter is placed in the centre of a hot pancake on the griddle, and it slides and glides across the surface as it melts.
expectation: The pat moves on a film of melted butter, slowing as it shrinks, and leaves a glossy trail; it does not stay put or refreeze.

caption: Boiling water is poured into a collapsed vacuum-packed camping meal pouch, and the pouch swells and stands up.
expectation: The pouch fills out as the water goes in and steam rises from its opening; it does not stay flat.

caption: A hairdryer is aimed at a wet patch on a bathroom mirror, and the patch shrinks from its edges.
expectation: The dry area spreads from where the warm air hits and the border of the wet patch retreats inward; the patch does not grow or reappear where it has dried.

caption: Wet footprints on a sun-baked pool deck dry in the heat, shrinking and fading from their edges.
expectation: Each print fades from its thin edges inward, the dark wet area getting smaller and lighter; prints do not darken, spread, or reappear once gone.

caption: An egg is cracked into a hot frying pan, and the clear white turns opaque white from the edges inward.
expectation: The white sets and whitens first where it touches the hot pan and the change spreads inward while the yolk stays yellow and domed; the set white does not turn clear again and the egg does not slide around as one piece before it sets.

caption: A drop of food colouring falls into each of two glasses side by side, one of hot water and one of cold, and the colour spreads through the hot water while it sinks in a thin thread in the cold.
expectation: In the hot glass the colour billows and spreads through the whole glass within seconds; in the cold glass it sinks as a thread and lingers near the bottom; the cold glass does not colour faster than the hot one.

caption: A glass thermometer is lowered into a mug of hot water, and its red column climbs.
expectation: The column starts rising as soon as the bulb is in the water, climbs steadily and slows as it settles; it does not fall, jump, or move before the bulb is wet.

caption: A limp balloon is stretched over the neck of an empty glass bottle, and the bottle is set in a bowl of hot water; the balloon begins to stand up and inflate.
expectation: The balloon lifts and swells slowly once the bottle is in the hot water and not before; it does not shrink or fill instantly.

caption: Boiling water is poured into a thick glass tumbler taken straight from the fridge, and the glass cracks with a sharp snap.
expectation: The crack appears within moments of the hot water going in and runs through the glass, which may split and leak; the glass does not stay whole or heal.

caption: Pancake batter is poured onto a hot griddle, and the pale liquid sets from the edge inward while small bubbles rise through its top.
expectation: The batter stops spreading and turns matte from the outside in, bubbles form and burst on the upper side, and the underside browns; the set part does not turn back to liquid.

caption: Grey raw shrimp are dropped into a hot pan, and they curl and turn pink.
expectation: Each shrimp tightens into a curve and its colour changes from translucent grey to opaque pink within seconds; the change starts on the side touching the pan and does not reverse.

caption: An iron rod rests with one end buried in the glowing coals of a forge, and the buried end begins to glow dull red and brightens toward orange.
expectation: The glow appears only on the part in the coals and spreads a short way along the rod; it grows brighter over time; the far end stays dark and the rod does not glow before it is heated.

caption: A layer of white sugar in a dry pan over heat melts from the edges into a clear liquid that turns amber and then deep brown.
expectation: The melting starts at the edges and works inward, the liquid darkens steadily from clear to amber to brown with thin smoke at the end; the colour never lightens and the liquid does not turn back into grains.

caption: A flat bag of microwave popcorn lies in a running microwave, and the bag swells and puffs up as popping begins inside.
expectation: The bag stays flat at first, then rises and rounds out while the pops come faster; it does not inflate before the popping starts or flatten while the popping goes on.

caption: A cold egg is lowered into a pot of boiling water, and its shell cracks and a thread of white leaks out and sets into a pale wisp.
expectation: The crack appears after the egg is in the water, the white streams out through it and turns opaque and solid in the hot water; the wisp does not dissolve or go back into the shell.

caption: An inflated balloon drifts down onto a burning candle, and it bursts the instant the flame touches it.
expectation: The balloon is whole until it meets the flame and disappears into shreds at that instant; the candle keeps burning; the balloon does not float through the flame or deflate slowly.
